original_question: Let T012(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which left stones are allowed, right stones are forbidden, and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T012(3n+1, 3n+2) = 2^n n! for every n >= 1?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3 ("Left stones, two kinds of bones") of arXiv:2206.06472.
correct_elements: Your draft targets exactly the right statement: Problem 3 in Section 3. It has the correct tiling type (type 012: right stones forbidden, left stones allowed, two bone types allowed), the correct benzel specialization ((3n+1, 3n+2)), the correct claimed enumeration (2^n n! = (2n)!!), and the correct quantifier n >= 1.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should define the (a,b)-benzel itself rather than only naming it.

It should use the paper’s formal notation T_{ijk}(a,b): for 0 <= i,j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3, T_{ijk}(a,b) counts tilings in which the right stone is allowed iff i=1, the left stone is allowed iff j=1, and exactly k of the three bone orientations are allowed.

The paper makes explicit that, by the benzel’s threefold rotational symmetry, the count depends only on how many bone types are allowed, not on which two; so one may equivalently fix the two allowed bones to be the rising and falling bones.
The paper works with the symmetry convention T_{ijk}(a,b)=T_{ijk}(b,a) and typically reduces to 2 <= a <= b <= 2a; your specific pair (3n+1,3n+2) with n >= 1 already lies in that range.
The paper’s own phrasing uses the double-factorial notation (2n)!!, together with the identity (2n)!! = 2^n n!.
refined_question: Let omega = exp(2pi i/3). For positive integers a,b satisfying 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a, the (a,b)-benzel is the union of the unit hexagonal cells lying fully inside the hexagon with vertices a omega + b, -a omega^2 - b, a omega^2 + b omega, -a - b omega, a + b omega^2, and -a omega - b omega^2. For 0 <= i,j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3, let T_{ijk}(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which the right stone is allowed iff i=1, the left stone is allowed iff j=1, and exactly k of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that, for every integer n >= 1, T_{012}(3n+1,3n+2) = (2n)!! = 2^n n!?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, since only the number of allowed bone orientations matters, is it true that for every n >= 1 the (3n+1,3n+2)-benzel has exactly (2n)!! tilings by left stones, rising bones, and falling bones?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem 3 in Section 3 of the paper. I did not replace it with the broader neighboring statement combining Problems 2 and 3. The refinements only make explicit the benzel definition, the formal definition of T_{ijk}(a,b), the symmetry fact that renders the choice of the two bone orientations immaterial, and the paper’s preferred notation (2n)!!.

citations.label: Definition of T_{ijk}(a,b), rotational-symmetry reduction, and dependence only on the number of allowed bone types
